seo.title: 30 Common Mistakes Web3 Frontend Developers Make (And How to Avoid Them)
seo.description: Learn from the mistakes of others. A comprehensive guide to the most common errors Web3 frontend developers make in wallet integration, state management, and UX.

content.intro: Web3 frontend development has unique challenges around wallet connections, transaction handling, and blockchain state. Here are the mistakes that trip up most developers.

items.title: Assuming wallet is always connected
items.description: Not handling disconnected state leads to crashes and poor UX.
items.solution: Always check connection state. Show appropriate UI for each state.

items.title: Not handling chain switching
items.description: Users switching networks in wallet breaks app if not handled.
items.solution: Listen for chain changes. Prompt users to switch back or adapt UI.

items.title: Only supporting one wallet
items.description: MetaMask-only apps exclude mobile users and hardware wallet users.
items.solution: Use RainbowKit or Web3Modal to support multiple wallets.

items.title: Not persisting connection state
items.description: Users have to reconnect wallet on every page refresh.
items.solution: Use wagmi's auto-connect feature. Store connection preference.

items.title: Blocking UI during wallet prompts
items.description: User cannot do anything while waiting for wallet signature.
items.solution: Show loading state but allow cancellation. Timeout long requests.

items.title: Not showing transaction status
items.description: Users don't know if transaction succeeded, failed, or is pending.
items.solution: Show clear pending, success, and error states. Link to explorer.

items.title: No gas estimation before send
items.description: Transactions fail due to insufficient gas without warning.
items.solution: Simulate transactions before sending. Show estimated gas cost.

items.title: Ignoring transaction reverts
items.description: Silent failures leave users confused about what happened.
items.solution: Catch revert reasons and display human-readable error messages.

items.title: Not handling stuck transactions
items.description: Low gas transactions can hang indefinitely.
items.solution: Provide speedup/cancel options. Link to tools for stuck transactions.

items.title: Displaying raw error messages
items.description: Technical revert strings are meaningless to users.
items.solution: Map common errors to friendly messages. Log technical details.

items.title: Polling too frequently
items.description: Excessive RPC calls hit rate limits and waste resources.
items.solution: Use appropriate polling intervals. use websockets where available.

items.title: Not caching blockchain data
items.description: Re-fetching same data on every render wastes RPC calls.
items.solution: Use TanStack Query with wagmi for smart caching.

items.title: Stale data after transactions
items.description: UI shows old balances/state after user's transaction confirms.
items.solution: Invalidate queries after transaction success. Optimistic updates.

items.title: Mixing local and chain state incorrectly
items.description: Local state can diverge from blockchain causing confusion.
items.solution: Use blockchain as source of truth. Local state for pending only.

items.title: Not handling block reorgs
items.description: Confirmed transactions can be undone in reorgs.
items.solution: Wait for sufficient confirmations for important transactions.

items.title: Exposing private keys in frontend
items.description: Private keys in client-side code can be stolen.
items.solution: Never use private keys in frontend. Use wallet signatures only.

items.title: Not validating input before signing
items.description: Users might sign malicious transactions from manipulated UI.
items.solution: Validate all inputs. Show clear transaction details before signing.

items.title: Trusting URL parameters blindly
items.description: Phishing attacks can manipulate transaction parameters via URL.
items.solution: Validate and sanitize all URL parameters. Confirm with user.

items.title: No phishing protection
items.description: Users can be tricked by lookalike domains.
items.solution: Educate users. Consider ENS/domain verification features.

items.title: Storing sensitive data in localStorage
items.description: localStorage is accessible to any script on the domain.
items.solution: Never store private keys or sensitive tokens in localStorage.

items.title: No mobile responsiveness
items.description: Many users access dApps via mobile wallet browsers.
items.solution: Build mobile-first. Test in MetaMask Mobile, Rainbow, etc.

items.title: Complex onboarding for new users
items.description: Requiring wallet setup immediately loses potential users.
items.solution: Allow browsing without wallet. Consider embedded wallets for onboarding.

items.title: No loading states
items.description: Blockchain operations are slow. Empty states confuse users.
items.solution: Show skeletons and spinners. Explain why operations take time.

items.title: Displaying raw addresses
items.description: 0x742d35Cc6634C0532925a3b844Bc9e7595f0ab3 is unreadable.
items.solution: Show ENS names when available. Truncate addresses (0x742d...0ab3).

items.title: Not explaining gas
items.description: New users don't understand why they need ETH for transactions.
items.solution: Explain gas in simple terms. Show estimated costs in USD.

items.title: Not testing with real wallets
items.description: Mocked wallets behave differently than MetaMask.
items.solution: Test with real wallets on testnets. Use Synpress for E2E tests.

items.title: Hardcoding contract addresses
items.description: Makes deployment to different networks painful.
items.solution: Use environment variables or config files for addresses.

items.title: Using outdated libraries
items.description: Old versions of ethers/web3 have bugs and security issues.
items.solution: Keep dependencies updated. Consider migrating to viem/wagmi.

items.title: No error boundaries
items.description: One error crashes entire app instead of just affected component.
items.solution: Wrap components in error boundaries. Show fallback UI.

items.title: Ignoring TypeScript types
items.description: Using 'any' types leads to runtime errors.
items.solution: Use strict TypeScript. wagmi and viem have excellent types.

proTips: Most frontend exploits target the user, not the code. Think like a phisher.
Test with multiple wallets. MetaMask behavior differs from WalletConnect.
Log client-side errors to Sentry. Users will not report bugs.
